REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 27, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director

11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to approve or ratify travel expenses for City-related business.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1048, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 2.15 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO EXTEND THE TERMS OF OFFICE FOR ADVISORY BOARD,
  COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS ORIGINALLY APPOINTED TO A
  TWO-YEAR 2022-24 TERM, AND GENERALLY AMEND THE DATES OF SUCH
  TERMS (COUNCIL), inclusive of the following modifications (noted in bold and
  strikethrough text):

  Chapter 2.15 – Advisory Boards, Commissions, and Committees

  Section 2.15.010 Terms of Office

  (a) All City Council appointments to City of Cerritos Advisory Boards, Commissions, and
  Committees shall be for a term of two years commencing on July 1 of odd-numbered
  years the 1st day of the month after the Annual Mayoral Transition conducted in odd-
  numbered years to coincide with the City’s General Municipal Election cycle, or within
  ninety days thereof, whichever is earlier; or shall expire earlier if the Councilmember
  making the appointment ceases to hold office as a member of the Cerritos City Council.
  Persons appointed may be removed by action of the Councilmember making the
  appointment, subject to approval by the City Council, or by a majority vote of the City
  Council. Appointments may be extended pursuant to subsection (b) of this section;

  (b) The term of any regular member of any City of Cerritos Advisory Board, Commission,
  or Committee is automatically extended until their respective successors are appointed
  and qualified, for not more than ninety days, pending the qualification of his or her their
  successor, whichever is earlier;
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, February 27, 2025, 7:00 p.m.

  (c) If a vacancy shall occur otherwise than by expiration of term, it shall be filled by
  appointment for the unexpired portion of the term. Such appointment shall be made by
  the Councilmember making the original appointment, with the approval of the City
  Council; and

  (d) Notwithstanding subsection (b) of this section, for members serving the 2022-2024
  term only, the term of any regular member of any City of Cerritos Advisory Board,
  Commission, or Committee is automatically extended through and including the last day
  of the month in which the Mayor is selected pursuant to Section 404 of the Cerritos City
  Charter as part of the 2025 annual Mayoral Transition, pending the qualification of his or
  her their successor, or within ninety days thereof, whichever is earlier.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration by the City Council of the potential closure of one (1) entrance
  into the neighborhood accessed by Bigelow Street and Bos Street and one (1) entrance
  into the Morning Sun neighborhood accessed by Spinnaker Street, Islandia Avenue, and
  Park Street for public safety purposes (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Alex Estella expressed concern regarding public safety and requested the City Council
  consider taking further crime deterring measures.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding public safety and spoke in support of a
  neighborhood survey and the closure of one (1) point of access into the subject
  neighborhoods. He also expressed concern regarding dispatcher responses.

  Susy Vigil expressed concern regarding public safety and spoke in support of the closure
  of one (1) point of access into the subject neighborhoods. She also spoke regarding a
  petition circulated among the neighborhood supporting this action and requested the City
  explore alternate measures to increase safety.

  Rocky Pavone expressed concern regarding public safety and suggested the City install
  more surveillance cameras around the City.

  Adriana Timoney expressed concern regarding public safety and spoke in support of a
  crime analysis and traffic study.

  Elizabeth Boudreaux thanked the City Council for the City’s response to requests for
  public safety enhancements and requested the City continue to prioritize public safety
  matters.

  Vipul Vineet expressed concern regarding public safety and spoke in support of the
  closure of one (1) point of access into the subject neighborhoods.

  Adrian Ayub expressed concern regarding public safety.

  Yasmin Cortez expressed concern regarding public safety and commented in support of
  further enhancements to increase safety in the City.

  Sophia Tse expressed concern regarding public safety and commented in support of the
  closure of one (1) point of access into the subject neighborhoods.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting the Council/Agency
  members received full-text, unredacted copies of the three (3) written comment(s)
  submitted for Item 9A, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the
  official record. Requests for copies of the written comment(s) submitted for this meeting
  can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

(minutes continue on the next page)

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  ORIGINAL MOTION (DID NOT CARRY): It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by
  Johnson, to direct staff to:

  1. Conduct a survey of the impacted residents of the subject neighborhoods, in order to
  gauge resident interest in the closure of access of one (1) entry point of the
  neighborhoods;

  2. Consult with the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority to assess the risk factors
  of the potential closure of access of one (1) entry point of the neighborhoods; and

  3. Schedule an agenda report for City Council consideration at a future meeting,
  presenting the findings of the survey and risk assessment (COUNCIL).

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (ADOPTED): It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by
  Yokoyama, to direct staff to:

  1. As soon as feasible, temporarily close access of one (1) neighborhood entry point at
  Spinnaker Street and one (1) neighborhood entry point at Bigelow Street, for a period
  of four (4) months;

  2. Consult with the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority to assess the risk factors
  of the potential closure of access of one (1) entry point of the neighborhoods;

  3. Obtain for consideration, surveys conducted by the affected community members;
  and

  4. Send an informational letter to residents of the subject neighborhoods regarding the
  upcoming street closures (COUNCIL).

  Mayor Solanki recused himself from the vote on this item due to the proximity of his
  residence to one (1) of the subject streets pending temporary closure.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding services provided by Athens Services and

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize the Mayor to
  execute Amendment Two to the Integrated Solid Waste Management Services Agreement
  with Athens Services, for an amended term ending June 30, 2042, before which, from January

  Contractor a new Franchise for a term of ten (10) years commencing July 1, 2042 and to
  extend the term of the Agreement for a commensurate period, inclusive of the following
  amendments:

  1.  Acquisition of new vehicles;
  2.  Senate Bill 1383 compliance enhancements;
  3.  Increased servicing of bust stop containers;
